newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybean ends down on weak sentiment.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybean ends down on weak sentiment.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mostly down on Tuesday on weak sentiment, traders said.
The key November 1996 contract ended at 3,256 yuan ($392) tonne, rising 11 yuan. It opened at 3,280 yuan, hitting an intra-day high of 3,348 and a low of 3,240.
January fell 26 to 3,161, March seven to 3,198, May 80 to 3,300, July 40 to 3,310 and September 60 to 3,320.
Combined volume fell to 1,460 tonnes from 12,400.
Traders said poor technical charts hurt market sentiment and that few investors wanted to build long positions.
"Breaching of the 3,300-yuan level triggered panic selling, with most investors pessimistic of future trends," one trader said.
"Over-supply of spot soybean has cast a shadow on investors who want to hold long positions," he added.
Analysts expect soybean to continue falling in the next few days.
